title: Shopify Plus Cross-Border Repeat Customer Growth: The 149% Playbook
summary: Shopify Plus cross-border repeat customer growth analysed: the 149% repeat-rate and 400% cross-border benchmark, plus a replicable playbook for APAC D2C brands.
body_markdown:
**Quick Answer:** Shopify's case study on Her lip to reports a 149% increase in repeat customers and roughly 400% cross-border revenue growth after moving to Shopify Plus. The repeat-rate gain is the mechanism: localised currency, duty-inclusive pricing and in-language post-purchase comms make each new market compound rather than plateau.


---


Success here looks specific. A Japanese apparel brand sells to a customer in Taipei in local currency, at a price that already includes duty, with a confirmation email in the buyer's language — and that same customer orders again within 90 days without a discount code. That is Shopify Plus cross-border repeat customer growth in its working form: not a traffic number, but a second order from a foreign postcode.


*Related reading:*[Shopify Plus vs BigCommerce B2B Enterprise APAC 2026](https://branch8.com/posts/shopify-plus-vs-bigcommerce-b2b-enterprise-apac-2026)


*Related reading:*[Salesforce Agentforce Pricing Strategy: An APAC Buyer's Verdict](https://branch8.com/posts/salesforce-agentforce-pricing-strategy-apac-comparison)


The benchmark most APAC D2C teams are now chasing comes from Haruna Kojima's "Her lip to." Shopify's published case study reports a **149% increase in repeat customers** and roughly **400% growth in cross-border ecommerce** after the brand replatformed to Shopify Plus, according to Shopify's 2025 merchant case study (Shopify). Those two numbers belong together. Cross-border revenue that grows four-fold on first orders alone is a paid-acquisition treadmill. Cross-border revenue that grows four-fold *while* repeat rate more than doubles is a system — and it is the clearest public example of Shopify Plus cross-border repeat customer growth working as designed.

*Related reading:*[Enterprise Ecommerce AI Agent Trust Framework: An APAC Playbook](https://branch8.com/posts/enterprise-ecommerce-ai-agent-trust-framework)


This piece works backwards from that outcome — what structurally has to be true for a brand in Hong Kong, Singapore, Taipei, Sydney or Auckland to reproduce it, and where the honest constraints sit.


## The headline finding: repeat rate, not reach, carried the growth


Strip the case study down and the causal order matters. The 400% cross-border figure is the visible result. The 149% repeat-customer figure is the mechanism that made it affordable.


The economics are well-documented. Bain & Company's work with Fred Reichheld found that a **5% increase in customer retention can lift profits by 25% to 95%** depending on the sector, according to Bain & Company's retention research (Bain & Company). In cross-border, the effect is amplified, because the fixed costs you paid once — localisation, duty configuration, carrier integration, translated support macros — are amortised across every subsequent order from that market.


Put plainly: the first order in a new market is expensive. The fourth is nearly free. Most brands never get to the fourth because they treat international expansion as a marketing campaign rather than an operations build, and Shopify Plus cross-border repeat customer growth becomes a slogan rather than a measured outcome.


## Cross-border is the fastest-growing slice of a slowing market


The market context supports the bet. Shopify's own research cites cross-border ecommerce growing toward **more than $4.81 trillion by 2032** , with the cross-border B2C segment at **$1.51 trillion in 2024** and a projected CAGR above 20%, according to Shopify's *Cross Border Ecommerce Guide* (Shopify). UNCTAD's digital economy reporting consistently places Asia as the largest regional contributor to global online retail activity, according to UNCTAD's latest digital economy report (UNCTAD).


That matters for a Hong Kong or Singapore brand in a specific way: your domestic market is small, but your regional addressable market is not. A Hong Kong beauty brand with a 7.5 million-person home market and a 400 million-person reachable Asian market is in a structurally different position from a US DTC brand optimising within one country.


The reverse is also true, and underused. For US, UK and EU brands, APAC is not just a demand market — it is a viable operations hub. Hong Kong and Singapore both offer no-duty-on-most-goods import regimes, dense air freight, and 1–3 day delivery windows to Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Australia and Southeast Asia. Shopify's multi-location inventory and Markets configuration lets a single store serve a US warehouse and a Hong Kong 3PL without duplicating the storefront.

## Localisation drives the repeat rate more than price does


The single most reliable lever on cross-border repeat purchase is language and currency, not discounting.


CSA Research's long-running "Can't Read, Won't Buy" study found that **76% of online shoppers prefer to buy products with information in their own language** , and **40% will not buy at all** from sites in other languages, according to CSA Research's most recent findings (CSA Research). That is a first-order constraint, not a nice-to-have.


Baymard Institute's aggregate of 49 studies puts average documented **cart abandonment at 70.2%** , with unexpected extra costs — shipping, duties, taxes — consistently ranking as the top stated reason among users who abandon for non-browsing reasons, according to Baymard Institute's 2025 analysis (Baymard Institute). In cross-border, "unexpected extra costs" is a duty problem, and duty is solvable at the configuration layer.


Shopify Markets handles the mechanics: per-market domains or subfolders, local currency with rounding rules, market-specific price lists, and duties-included (DDP) presentation at checkout. On Plus, you can also run market-specific checkout branding and Shopify Functions for market-specific shipping and discount logic. This is the configuration layer that underwrites any serious Shopify Plus cross-border repeat customer growth plan.


A minimal check of whether your markets are actually configured — not just enabled:


```text
1  # Shopify Admin API 2025-07 — audit market configuration    2  query MarketAudit {    3    markets(first: 20) {    4      nodes {    5        name    6        handle    7        enabled    8        primary    9        webPresence { domain { host } subfolderSuffix }    10        currencySettings {    11          baseCurrency { currencyCode }    12          localCurrencies    13        }    14        regions(first: 20) { nodes { ... on MarketRegionCountry { code } } }    15      }    16    }    17  }
```


If` localCurrencies` is` false` on a market doing meaningful volume, you are paying for traffic and then taxing it at checkout with an unfamiliar currency. Fix that before you fix anything else.


## Repeat rate must be measured per market, not in aggregate


This is where most reporting fails. A blended repeat-purchase rate of 28% can hide a 41% rate in Japan and a 9% rate in Australia — and the 9% is usually a fulfilment or returns problem, not a product problem.


Shopify Plus gives you the raw material through customer and order segmentation; the discipline is cohorting by *market of first order* , then measuring 90-day and 180-day repurchase.


```text
1  # Orders by market for cohort construction    2  query OrdersByMarket($cursor: String) {    3    orders(first: 250, after: $cursor, query: "created_at:>2025-01-01") {    4      pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }    5      nodes {    6        createdAt    7        customer { id numberOfOrders createdAt }    8        shippingAddress { countryCodeV2 }    9        currencyCode    10        totalPriceSet { shopMoney { amount } presentmentMoney { amount currencyCode } }    11      }    12    }    13  }
```


Pull that into your warehouse, pivot on` countryCodeV2` × first-order month, and you have a cross-border repeat customer growth rate you can actually act on. We have built exactly this cohort view for a Greater China multi-brand retail group selling into Japan and Southeast Asia; the useful finding was never the blended number — it was which single market's repeat rate was being suppressed by a returns policy nobody had translated.

## Four configuration decisions explain most of the gap


Across replatforming work in Hong Kong, Taiwan and Australia, the same four decisions separate brands that compound internationally from brands that plateau.


### Duties presented, not discovered


DDP at checkout, with landed cost shown before payment. Shopify Managed Markets (where available) or a third-party calculator via Shopify Functions. The trade-off is real: DDP costs margin and adds reconciliation work. It also removes the single most common cause of a first-time international buyer never returning — a courier invoice arriving after delivery.


### Local payment methods, not just cards


Shopify Payments now supports a wide set of countries — Shopify has publicly cited availability across **39 markets** in recent merchant communications — and Shopify Plus merchants can layer local methods: Konbini and JCB for Japan, PayNow for Singapore, FPS and AlipayHK for Hong Kong, Grab/ShopeePay rails via gateways in Southeast Asia. Card-only checkout in Japan or Indonesia is a self-inflicted conversion ceiling.


### Delivery promise stated in local terms


"Ships from Hong Kong, arrives Tokyo in 2–4 business days" converts and retains better than "international shipping available." Specificity is the retention feature.


### Post-purchase comms in-language


Translated transactional emails, returns instructions, and at least macro-level support coverage. This is the cheapest of the four and the most frequently skipped.


## Shopify's platform trajectory supports the bet — with caveats


Two of the questions buyers actually ask before committing deserve direct answers.


**Is Shopify growing or shrinking?** Growing. Shopify reported Q2 2025 revenue of roughly **$2.68 billion, up about 31% year over year** , on GMV of approximately **$87.8 billion, up about 31%** (Shopify Investor Relations). Cross-border GMV has been reported by Shopify as a meaningful and rising share of total GMV — the company has repeatedly flagged international as a growth vector in quarterly commentary.


**What does Shopify take from a $100 sale?** On standard plans with Shopify Payments, roughly **2.9% + $0.30** in the US — about $3.20, leaving $96.80 before your own costs. Shopify Plus negotiates lower card rates, typically in the 2.2–2.5% range depending on volume and region, but adds a platform fee structured as a variable percentage of GMV above the base subscription. Cross-border adds currency conversion (commonly around 1.5%) and, if you use a third-party gateway instead of Shopify Payments, an additional platform transaction fee. Model the all-in rate for your actual market mix, not the headline card rate.


The caveat: Plus is not the cheapest route to international selling. For brands under roughly US$2–3 million in annual GMV with a single market, standard Shopify plus apps usually wins on total cost. Plus earns its premium when you need multiple markets, B2B alongside D2C, checkout extensibility, and the higher API limits that make the cohort reporting above practical.

## The replicable playbook, in sequence


From the Her lip to pattern and what we see in APAC replatforms, the order of operations matters more than the tooling:


1. **Pick two markets, not eight.** Depth beats breadth. Full localisation in Japan and Taiwan outperforms shallow presence in ten countries.
2. **Localise before you advertise.** Currency, language, duty, payment methods, delivery promise — then spend.
3. **Instrument repeat rate per market from day one.** You cannot improve what you only see blended.
4. **Fix the second-order experience.** Returns, exchanges, reorder flows, loyalty in local currency.
5. **Only then scale spend.** Acquisition into a market with a proven 90-day repeat rate is investment; acquisition into an unproven one is a test, and should be budgeted as one.


A credible Shopify Plus cross-border repeat customer growth plan has a per-market repeat-rate target attached to each stage. Without that, you have a launch checklist, not a growth programme.


## What to do Monday morning


1. **Run the market audit query.** Pull your Shopify markets configuration and flag any market with meaningful order volume where local currency, local payment methods, or DDP duty presentation is switched off. That list is your backlog, ranked by GMV.
2. **Build the per-market repeat cohort.** Export 12 months of orders segmented by first-order country and calculate 90-day repurchase rate per market. Identify your best and worst market — the delta is your diagnosis.
3. **Read your own post-purchase emails in a non-English market.** Open the actual order confirmation, shipping notification, and returns instructions a Japanese or Taiwanese customer receives. If any of them are in English, you have found a retention leak you can close this week.
